newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH turns higher, share block trades.
newsitem.headline: LVMH turns higher, share block trades.

text.p: Shares in French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH reversed earlier losses and added 3.59 percent to 1,357 francs at 1047 GMT. The market was down 0.76 percent.
A block of 113,000 shares traded at 1,324 francs per share at 1024 GMT, market sources said.

One broker said the market liked LVMH's plan to extend the goodwill writedown of its DFS acquisition to 40 years as this would be earnings-positive. Chairman Bernard Arnault's presentation to analysts gave a "very positive outlook for 1997," he added. LVMH earlier posted 1996 net attributable profit of 3.68 billion francs.

The broker added that the analysts' meeting had led some to a revaluation of the shares, which have recently underperformed, and who now consider it a good quality stock. That has contributed to a technical correction, he added.

But another trader said the market was only focusing on the company's positives and disregarding the downside, such as the weaker than expected operating profit. Bids on the stock were in not especially big volumes.
Another market source said there was scepticism over where the company's promised strong growth would come from and its strategy with DFS for developing Asian markets.
